scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Act lawfully and within vires under the Procurement Act 2023
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs due to automatic suspension
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Deliver £112,100,000 worth of AC traction motors and control equipment for London Underground's critical services
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in the procurement process
Minimising Litigation Risk: Provide enough disclosure to reassure Alstom without undermining evaluation confidentiality or integrity
goals: Defend the procurement decision, maintain contract continuity and protect public funds
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: The evaluation process was conducted fairly and lawfully, and the award to Bombardier was made in accordance with the mandatory technical threshold requirement.
legal_basis: Regulation 32(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million worth of contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: alleged manifest error in applying technical threshold requirement
Protection of Reputation: potential damage to our credibility and win-rate targets
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids, giving us a chance to be awarded the contract ourselves
An award of damages for any financial harm suffered due to the alleged manifest error
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We will not agree to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework without assurance that our concerns regarding the manifest error are addressed

messages.message: Alstom Transport UK Ltd has challenged our evaluation of their bid for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment, alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement. We understand that this challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. However, we would like to clarify whether Alstom Transport UK Ltd is suggesting that our evaluation team misapplied the technical threshold requirement, or if they are disputing the requirement itself. Could you please provide more information on their specific concerns regarding the technical threshold?

We appreciate your clarification request and would like to know more about the specific technical threshold requirement that you applied during evaluation. Can you provide us with a detailed breakdown of how this requirement was implemented, including any relevant scoring matrices or documentation? We believe it's essential to understand the exact methodology used to assess our bid against this requirement.

We appreciate your request for detailed breakdown of the technical threshold requirement. We can provide you with a copy of the evaluation scoring matrix, which clearly outlines how we applied the mandatory technical threshold requirement to each bid. Specifically, Section 3.2 of the scoring matrix details the weightage assigned to this criterion and how it was used to evaluate Bombardier's bid. We also confirm that our evaluation team followed the exact methodology outlined in the tender documentation when assessing the bids against this requirement. However, we would like to clarify whether Alstom Transport UK Ltd is disputing the technical threshold requirement itself or just its application in their case.

We appreciate your clarification on the technical threshold requirement and the provision of the evaluation scoring matrix. However, we are concerned that our bid was unfairly disadvantaged by an inconsistent application of this requirement. We would like to request a more detailed explanation of how Bombardier's bid met the technical threshold, particularly in light of the fact that our own bid exceeded the minimum requirements specified in the tender documentation. Furthermore, we believe it is essential to understand why our bid did not receive the same treatment as Bombardier's, despite meeting or exceeding all mandatory criteria.
messages.proposal: A re-evaluation of our bid against the technical threshold requirement, with a focus on ensuring consistency and fairness

messages.message: We acknowledge Alstom Transport UK Ltd's concerns regarding the inconsistent application of the technical threshold requirement and their bid exceeding the minimum requirements specified in the tender documentation. We can provide additional feedback on how our evaluation team applied the technical threshold to each bid, including a detailed comparison between Bombardier's and Alstom Transport UK Ltd's bids. However, we must clarify that our evaluation team followed the exact methodology outlined in the tender documentation when assessing the bids against this requirement. We are willing to provide a voluntary standstill extension for engagement to address these concerns and provide further clarification on our evaluation process.

We appreciate your offer to provide additional feedback on how your evaluation team applied the technical threshold requirement to each bid, including a detailed comparison between Bombardier's and Alstom Transport UK Ltd's bids. However, we are concerned that this may not be sufficient to address our concerns regarding the inconsistent application of this requirement. We propose that you conduct a re-evaluation of both bids against the technical threshold requirement, using an independent evaluation team or panel to ensure objectivity and fairness.
messages.proposal: Re-evaluation of both bids by an independent evaluation team

compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, as it involves a technical threshold requirement and its application. I will assess the Contracting Authority's process based on rationality and compliance with the published criteria. The technical threshold requirement is mandatory, which means that any bid failing to meet this requirement should be excluded from further evaluation. However, without specific details on how this requirement was implemented or the scoring matrices used, it is difficult to determine if a manifest error occurred. I will proceed under the assumption that the Contracting Authority has followed a rational process in applying the technical threshold requirement.

applicable_provisions: s.12 Procurement Act 2023 (value for money, public benefit, transparency, integrity)
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative as it involves a technical threshold requirement and its application to bids. The Contracting Authority provided the evaluation scoring matrix, which outlines how they applied the mandatory technical threshold requirement to each bid. However, I do not have enough information to perform a calculation or verify the scores. Therefore, I will assess compliance qualitatively. The Contracting Authority claims that their evaluation team followed the exact methodology outlined in the tender documentation when assessing the bids against this requirement. This is rationally defensible and does not contradict the published criteria's plain wording.

applicable_provisions: s12 Procurement Act 2023 (value for money, public benefit, transparency, integrity)
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative as it involves a technical threshold requirement and its application to bids. The Contracting Authority claims they followed the exact methodology outlined in the tender documentation when assessing the bids against this requirement. However, Alstom Transport UK Ltd alleges a manifest error in applying this requirement. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead of performing an arithmetic calculation. The Contracting Authority's willingness to provide additional feedback and clarification on their evaluation process suggests they are attempting to be transparent and address concerns. However, the Aggrieved Bidder is concerned that this may not be sufficient to address their concerns regarding inconsistent application of the technical threshold requirement.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome of a re-evaluation was more favorable than our initial BATNA, which would have involved defending against Alstom's challenge in TCC court, potentially resulting in significant costs (£50k+) and time (6-12 months). The re-evaluation allowed us to address Alstom's concerns and provide additional clarity on our evaluation process without the need for a lengthy and costly legal battle.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a re-evaluation of both bids, which provided an opportunity for Alstom Transport UK Ltd to have their concerns addressed. Although we did not achieve a full win in terms of having the challenge dismissed, the outcome was still favorable as it avoided the risks and costs associated with defending against Alstom's challenge in TCC court.
what_was_achieved: Provided additional feedback on how our evaluation team applied the technical threshold requirement to each bid
Offered a voluntary standstill extension for engagement to address concerns and provide further clarification
what_was_conceded: Agreed to re-evaluate both bids against the technical threshold requirement using an independent evaluation team or panel
Provided a detailed breakdown of the technical threshold requirement, including the scoring matrix and methodology used

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is slightly better than our BATNA (pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings), but still not ideal. We were able to secure a re-evaluation of both bids, which may lead to a more favorable outcome for us.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a re-evaluation of the technical threshold requirement, which may result in a revised evaluation that favors our bid. This is a partial win, as it addresses some of our concerns and provides an opportunity for a more objective assessment.
what_was_achieved: A re-evaluation of both bids against the technical threshold requirement
Additional feedback on how the evaluation team applied the technical threshold to each bid
what_was_conceded: The contracting authority's initial position that damages would be an adequate remedy for us if we succeeded at trial
Their insistence on proceeding with the contract despite our challenge during the standstill period

key_sticking_points: Application of mandatory technical threshold requirement
Inconsistent treatment of Alstom Transport UK Ltd's bid compared to Bombardier's
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority provided additional feedback and clarification on their evaluation process, including a detailed comparison between the two bids. However, they refused to conduct an independent re-evaluation as proposed by the Aggrieved Bidder.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, focusing on rationality and compliance with published criteria. The Court did not find any manifest errors in the Contracting Authority's process but recommended a re-evaluation due to concerns about inconsistent application of the technical threshold requirement.
summary.likely_next_steps: Re-evaluation of both bids against the technical threshold requirement using an independent evaluation team or panel, as proposed by the Aggrieved Bidder.
summary.plain_english_summary: The dispute centered around how the Contracting Authority applied a mandatory technical requirement to two bids. The Aggrieved Bidder claimed they were unfairly disadvantaged compared to Bombardier's bid. Despite some concessions from the Contracting Authority, the Court recommended re-evaluation due to concerns about inconsistent treatment.
